analysis:
This PR adds an 'excluded shape warmup' to the provider: ProviderLoop+ModelCalibration.swift:17-24 (falls back to startShapeWarmupIfNeeded when calibration doesn't start), ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift:237 and 346-350 (new shapeWarmup dependency, guarded by Task cancellation, shutdown, servingDrain and unloading checks), StandaloneServer+StartupPreload.swift:42 and 50-74 (standalone warmup and a retry scheduler), and StandaloneServer.swift:549-554 (the KV sweep task now holds self weakly and calls retryShapeWarmups, gated on lifecycleState == .running and not draining).

Security-relevant observations: the changes only add local engine warmup scheduling. They add no new network input, no consumer data, no key handling, no attestation or authorization surface, and no disk artifacts. Warmup implementations (runShapeWarmupBeforeServing, startShapeWarmupIfNeeded) are in files not supplied. I could not verify whether the warmup uses synthetic prompts only, or whether it writes into the encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041). If warmup donations reached the SSD cache, they would be synthetic and the at-rest exposure would be unchanged in kind. The startup gate's timeout still bounds registration delay (availability, T-010/T-029). The weak self capture in the sweep task avoids a retain cycle. Open questions for integration: (1) that startup warmup is bounded or cancellable when serving drains mid-warmup, since only a pre-start guard is visible; (2) that warmup does not hold device-work receipts or GPU residency that interferes with the idle-unload policy (T-029) or with App Attest native-call admission or draining. No concrete regression is evident from the supplied evidence.
